note: UPGRADED FROM THE FALLBACK: this table now ships the ADMINISTERED POLISH. It originally shipped English in the base fields as translated_substitute, on the finding that the Polish was in neither the deposit nor the paper. It is in neither -- but it IS in the Polish adaptation the paper cites, Grzesiak-Feldman (2012), whose Zalacznik 1 lists a 20-item 'Skala Prawicowego Autorytaryzmu'. All twelve items this study administered appear there verbatim. So Polish takes item_text, the .sav's English labels move to item_text_translated (the authors' own renderings, hence translation_source=study_supplied), and text_source becomes study_materials. THE PAIRING IS FORCED BY CONTENT, not position: each of the twelve English labels is a direct translation of exactly one numbered appendix item and vice versa, drawn from a pool of twenty. The map is rwa1<-13, rwa2<-2, rwa3<-8, rwa4<-4, rwa5<-9, rwa6<-1, rwa7<-14, rwa8<-7, rwa9<-12, rwa10<-6, rwa11<-11, rwa12<-3, so the study used appendix items 1-4, 6-9 and 11-14 and none of 5, 10 or 15-20. THE QUESTIONNAIRE ALTERNATED KEYING: the six items the appendix marks (R) land exactly on the odd codes rwa1, rwa3, rwa5, rwa7, rwa9, rwa11 -- the same alternating design the cons block shows, where odd items are one subscale and even the other. CORRECTS A CLAIM THIS TABLE ORIGINALLY SHIPPED. Its first public note said the items are 'stored RAW'. They are not. Solving for the weights of the deposit's own rwa_sum returns +1 on all twelve with a zero intercept, reproducing it for 342 of 342 complete rows; flipping the six reverse-worded items instead reproduces only 22 of 342. So the deposit stores them ALREADY RECODED, with higher meaning more authoritarian for every item. A consequence worth stating: keying polarity therefore cannot be used to test the pairing on this table -- all twelve intercorrelate positively, across-block r = +0.160 rather than negative -- and that is explained by the recoding rather than being a failure of the mapping. RESPONSE ANCHORS STILL NOT SHIPPED, and the new source is the reason to be careful rather than bolder: the appendix publishes a SIX-point scale ('(1) Zdecydowanie sie nie zgadzam' through '(6) Zdecydowanie sie zgadzam'), but this study administered FIVE points -- the paper says 5-point and the live data contains only 1-5. So the appendix's labels do not describe this administration and option_text stays blank. PROVENANCE CORRECTED -- text_source WAS study_materials AND IS NOW canonical_instrument, because the Polish shipped here is NOT established as the administered wording. Reading Radkiewicz (2011) properly shows the two are different Polish adaptations of RWA. Radkiewicz says of his own appendix: 'W badaniu zastosowano wersje zawierajaca 20 pozycji, wzorowana na tej, ktorej uzywal w swoich badaniach Duckitt' -- a 20-item version modelled on Duckitt, from Altemeyer's original. He cites Funke twice and Grzesiak-Feldman not at all. The lys study, by contrast, cites Funke (2005) adapted to Polish by Grzesiak-Feldman (2012), 12 items on three factors. So the appendix is an Altemeyer/Duckitt-lineage Polish RWA while the study administered a Funke-lineage one. WHAT IS STILL SOLID: the twelve items correspond in CONTENT, and that correspondence is not loose -- each of the .sav's twelve English labels is a direct translation of exactly one appendix item out of twenty, and independently the lys paper's own three RWA example items (one per factor) all appear in the appendix, as items 03, 02 and 04. Funke's 12-item scale is itself built from Altemeyer's pool, which is why the content overlaps. WHAT IS NOT SOLID: whether the Polish STRINGS are the ones respondents read. Grzesiak-Feldman's adaptation may word the same items differently, and her paper was not consulted. The close English-to-Polish fit is good evidence the two adaptations share wording, but it is evidence and not identity. NOTE THE RESULTING INVERSION, which is worth stating plainly: for this table the ENGLISH in item_text_translated is the more authoritative record of what was administered, because it comes from the study's own .sav, while the Polish in item_text is a published rendering of the same items from a sibling adaptation. Closing this needs Grzesiak-Feldman (2012) itself.

source_ref: Deposit workbook 'Knowledge and Fear of COVID-19 and Perceived Stress.xlsb' (osf.io/m2v3h) -- its 'Codebook' sheet keys Q1..Q12 to their statements and states '0 - Incorrect; 1 - Correct', its 'Survey 1' sheet carries the same twelve statements with the True/False answer key and a % Correct column, and its 'DataSet' sheet holds the response columns; data/kfcovid_Li2020/'knowledge and fear of covid_ knowledge scale.do' for the code derivation. Article: Li & Leung (2020), Data in Brief 33:106395, CC BY, PMC7546663.
note: Level 1 with the mapping mechanical rather than inferred, despite bare-integer item codes. The live codes are 1-12, which normally calls for reconstruction caution, but data/kfcovid_Li2020/'knowledge and fear of covid_ knowledge scale.do' reshapes `Q1 Q2 ... Q12 -> Q` and renames the reshape index to `item`, so the integer IS the Q number; the deposit workbook's Codebook sheet then keys each Q to its statement. TWO SHEETS CROSS-CHECK EACH OTHER: the Codebook and Survey 1 statements are byte-identical for 11 of the 12, and the twelfth is recoverable only from Survey 1 because the Codebook's Q4 cell is a broken spreadsheet reference rendering as '0x17'. That item is 'Only those who are elderly, have chronic illnesses, and/ or are obese could suffer severe symptoms as a result of COVID-19.' EXTRACTION NOTE: the deposit is an Excel BINARY workbook (.xlsb), which openpyxl cannot read and no office converter was available; it was read positionally with pyxlsb. An earlier attempt that harvested UTF-16 strings out of the raw sheet bytes silently lost that same Q4 item, so the positional read matters. VERIFICATION: the workbook publishes % Correct per item and the observed proportion of resp == 1 reproduces all twelve to 0.000e+00 -- see verify_kfcovid_Li2020.R. Instrument provenance: the article says the twelve were 'adapted from' Zhong et al. (2020), Int J Biol Sci 16:1745, so the wording shipped here is this study's own as deposited, not Zhong's. WHAT resp MEANS, and it is the thing a user must not misread. Respondents chose among THREE options -- 'True, false, I don't know' -- but the table does not store that choice. It stores CORRECTNESS, 0 for incorrect and 1 for correct, per the Codebook sheet. That is proven rather than assumed: for each of the four False-keyed items the observed share of resp == 1 equals the published % Correct exactly, so item 9 (a False statement) shows 0.9909 where a literal-answer coding would show 0.0091. THE ANSWER KEY, for the record: items 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 10, 11 and 12 are TRUE statements; items 4, 5, 6 and 9 are FALSE statements. WHY option_text AND correct_response ARE BOTH BLANK, after two wrong attempts. They first shipped as option_text = 'Incorrect'/'Correct' with correct_response = 1. Both were wrong: 'Correct' is a SCORING LABEL, not a response option available to anyone, and the standard reserves option_text for 'the literal text for a specific response option available for an item' with resp being 'the response value assigned to a specific option_text'; meanwhile '1' on a true/false item reads as 'the answer is True', which is false for items 4, 5, 6 and 9. This is the standard's 'may legitimately be missing for behavior-scored items' case, so both are empty and the answer key and option list live here and in the public note instead. AND WHY raw_resp IS NOT USED, since it was tried and reverted. A version shipped the three administered options in option_text and raw_resp with resp left empty. That looked tidier and was worse: SKILL.md reserves raw_resp for when NO scoring key exists anywhere, warning that shipping label strings 'when the live table stores integers leaves the text unlinkable to any response'. The key does exist here -- the workbook publishes it -- and the effect was exactly as warned: the live 0/1 disappeared from the table and validate_items SKIPPED the resp check rather than passing it, so the join axis went unverified. resp now carries the live 0/1 and both axes pass.
public_note: Twelve true/false COVID-19 knowledge statements. resp is NOT the respondent's answer: respondents chose among three options -- 'True', 'false' and 'I don't know' -- and the table stores only whether they were right, 0 for incorrect and 1 for correct. option_text is therefore blank, because 'Incorrect' and 'Correct' are scoring labels rather than options anyone could select, and correct_response is blank because a correctness axis has no key to state -- a '1' there would read as 'the answer is True', which is wrong for the four false statements. Whether each statement is itself true or false: items 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 10, 11 and 12 are TRUE statements; items 4, 5, 6 and 9 are FALSE statements. Item codes are the source workbook's Q numbers. n = 110 Filipino domestic workers in Hong Kong, July 2020.

Measures' -- Codebook_Baseline.xlsx rows 124-137 carry all fourteen items with a per-item response ladder in its Values column; data/mhscdc_fried_2020.r line 61 for the code derivation. Preprint: Fried & Epskamp (2022), 'Mental Health and Social Contact During the COVID-19 Pandemic: An Ecological Momentary Assessment Study', doi:10.31234/osf.io/36xkp, deposit CC BY. SAS-SV source: Kwon, Kim, Cho & Yang (2013), PLoS ONE 8(12):e83558, CC BY.
note: THE SMARTPHONE BLOCK IS IN THE BASELINE CODEBOOK, NOT THE EMA ONE, which is the first thing to know about this table: the study is an ecological-momentary-assessment design and the deposit ships Codebook_EMA.xlsx, Codebook_Post.xlsx and Codebook_Baseline.xlsx, but searching the EMA codebook for these items returns nothing. All fourteen live here in Baseline. MAPPING is a number-preserving rename with nothing positional in it: the codebook's cleandata_pre column names them Q102..Q115, and data/mhscdc_fried_2020.r calls process_dass_data(bt_df, "Pre", 102, 115, ...) which selects num_range("Pre", 102:115) and pivots with names_to = "item", so the live code is the source column name and its number is the codebook's Q number. TWO BLOCKS, FIVE DIFFERENT LADDERS. Section 1 is the ten-item Smartphone Addiction Scale - Short Version on a single 6-point agree/disagree ladder. Section 2 is four study-specific general-use items, each with its OWN ladder of a different length: duration of use (6), frequency of use (6), time to first use in the morning (4), and function with most personal relevance (8). The codebook's Values cell is populated only on the first row of each block and inherited down, which the extraction handles explicitly. CORROBORATION: every item's observed response range falls inside its own codebook ladder, and the ladder lengths are a distinctive fingerprint -- Pre114 tops out at exactly 4 while Pre112 and Pre115 stop short of their 6 and 8 because two offered levels went unchosen (Pre112 '6 = More than 6 hours' and Pre115 '8 = Reading news'). Those two unused levels are why the live table shows a maximum resp of 7 and why IRW metadata records 7 categories despite one item offering eight. PRE115 IS NOMINAL and this is a data-standard concern rather than an item-text one: its resp values are arbitrary category codes for which smartphone function a respondent named, so they are not ordinal and should not be treated as a scale. The codebook itself marks its measurement level Nominal, unlike every other item here. Ladder parsing note: several option labels contain digits ('11-60 minutes', '6-10 times', 'within 6-30 minutes'), so the ladders were split only at a number matching the next expected level, never at a digit inside a label. RIGHTS: clears the test positively rather than by silence. note: ITEM TEXT IS THE TASK DESCRIPTION, NOT A LITERAL SUM, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE REFUSAL rather than a gap. The deposit ships FOUR parallel forms of this test (Math 3-5_Form1..Form4, plus four '3-5 testing booklet_sample*' booklets) and their content differs -- the four PDFs are pairwise non-identical and their numeral sequences differ. The live table records no form: its columns are cluster_id, wave, cov_female, cov_age, cov_grade, treat, e2_std12, e2_std35, test and item_grade, none of which identifies which booklet a child received. So no literal problem is a property of an item code. The English form that IS readable ('Math 3-5_Mar27_Form1eng.doc', headed 'MATHS (3-5) TEST 1') contains concrete sums -- 36 + 61, 678 + 923, 98 - 55, 238 - 129, 6971 + 5291, 'What is the place value of 9740?' -- and shipping those as item_text would assert content that roughly three quarters of respondents never saw. The task description is what the source ties to the code and it is what ships. CONSEQUENCE a user should expect: item_text repeats across a task family. Five items read 'Multiplication', five 'Solve the sums', four 'Addition(2-3 digit)', four 'Subtraction(2-3 digit)', three each 'Division' and 'Word Problem'. That is the source's granularity, not an extraction failure. MAPPING: live codes are the deposit's variable names with the wave prefix (b_ baseline, e1_/e2_ endline) stripped, and the live `wave` column (0, 0.5, 1) carries what the prefix encoded. The dictionary's 36 codes and the live 36 are the same set exactly. The renaming itself happened upstream of this repo -- data/gilbert_hte/postprocessing.R points at an external 'gilbert_share/06 IL-HTE Econ/analysis/' -- so it was verified from the wave-availability pattern instead; see verify_gilbert_meta_73.R. THE TEST CHANGED BETWEEN WAVES, which is why 11 of the 36 codes are wave-restricted: hvy_obj ('Circle the heaviest object') and sol_a..sol_e ('Solve the sums') are baseline-only, and add3d_c, add3d_d, mul_d, mul_e and subt3d_d are endline-only. Question NUMBERING also differs between the baseline and endline forms because the baseline carried the five extra sol_* items -- add3d_a is q9a at baseline but q8a at endline, division is q15 against q14 -- so no single question number is canonical and none is shipped. RESP: 0/1, and the deposit carries no value labels for these variables, so option_text is blank rather than invented. That 1 means correct is not stated outright but follows from makedata.do recoding 9 to 0 and summing the items into test scores with rowtotal; it is recorded in the public note as an inference, not as a transcription. correct_response is empty because the correct answer is form-dependent and resp is already a correctness score.

IMPORTANT: item_text is the TASK the item asks, not the specific sum.
